question: The task label matches (binary MCI vs normal) but the channel does not: P-117 (correct PDF S1746809423008959, Aljalal et al.) uses resting-state EEG; P-50 (Wang, Liang et al., Neuroscience 557 (2024) 81-88) uses T1 structural MRI morphometry (cortical SBM + subcortical VBM/shape). Condition 1 fails on channel.
metric: Same metric type (accuracy), segment-level 10-fold CV (P-117) vs subject-level LOOCV (P-50).

figures.P-117: 99.81% accuracy (ensemble KNN, 11 NSGA-II channels; 99.51% all 19 channels), binary aMCI vs HC, 10-fold CV over 3660 segment feature vectors from 61 participants; no interval reported. Wilson 95% with n = 61: z^2/n = 0.06297; centre = (0.9981 + 0.03149)/1.06297 = 0.9686; half-width 0.0314; interval [0.937, 1.000].
figures.P-50: 89% accuracy (sensitivity 87%, specificity 90%, AUC 0.89), linear SVM, LOOCV, 46 participants (24 MCI/22 NC). No interval reported. Wilson with n = 46: z^2/n = 3.8415/46 = 0.08351; centre = (0.89 + 0.04175)/1.08351 = 0.8599; half-width = 1.96*sqrt(0.89*0.11/46 + 3.8415/(4*46^2))/1.08351 = 0.0919; interval [0.768, 0.952].

matched_figure_check: No matched figure exists. Neither paper reports a result in the other's channel, and P-117 prints no subject-level accuracy that would match P-50's LOOCV unit. Nothing reconciles the pair.
performance_validity: P-117 meets the Section 3.5 exclusion on its own PDF: 99.81% (>= 0.97), internal 10-fold CV over randomly split segment feature vectors, 61 participants, no external cohort. P-50's 89% is below the threshold and is not excluded.
reason: The numbers differ beyond uncertainty (0.9981 lies outside P-50's Wilson [0.768, 0.952]; 0.89 lies outside P-117's [0.937, 1.000]), but EEG and structural MRI are different measurement channels, so the pair does not address the same clinical question under condition 1. P-117's 99.81% also fails the performance-validity exclusion (condition 5). The record's figures match the papers; its dataset_equal='Yes' is wrong.

quotes.quote: With an ensemble KNN classifier, the highest accuracy, 99.81%, is achieved using 11 channels selected by an NSGA-based method.
The combined dataset has 61 people over the age of 55, including 29 amnestic MCI patients and 32 normal cases.

For evaluating the performance of each classifier, we employ 10-fold CV. This method randomly splits the dataset into ten equal subsets, with one subset used for validation (test) and the other nine for training
When combined with cortical and subcortical metrics, SVM achieved a peak accuracy of 89 % in distinguishing MCI from NC.
A total of 46 participants were included in the study, consisting of 24 MCI patients and 22 NCs.
SVM classification was based on a linear kernel function, and leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) was selected to evaluate the performance of the classification model
